title: Prevalence of nicotine product use among people with mental health conditions compared to the general population
summary: There has been a documented decline in nicotine consumption in recent years. It is well known that patients with psychiatric disorders consume nicotine at higher rates than the general population. Is there also a decline in nicotine consumption among people with psychiatric disorders, and how has consumption changed in terms of quantity and pattern. What reasons can be identified for the differences observed.

interventions.name: Patients with psychiatric disorders who are receiving inpatient or outpatient care at Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, LVR University Hospital Essen are asked to complete the “Smoke-Free Hospital Survey” questionnaire once to assess their smoking status and drug use.
Data from the “DEBRA – German Survey on Smoking Behavior” study are used as a comparison cohort representing the “psychiatrically healthy general population.”

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Adult patients receiving outpatient or inpatient treatment at the LVR-Klinikum Essen.
-Diagnosed (ICD-10) mental disorders, particularly opioid dependence, alcohol dependence, cannabis dependence, depressive disorders, schizophrenia-spectrum psychoses, and anxiety disorders.
Exclusion criteria:
-Insufficient understanding of the German language to comprehend the patient information and ensure that the interview can be conducted adequately.
-Severe cognitive impairments, e.g., Korsakoff syndrome, progression of dementia
-Acute psychiatric illness (e.g., active psychotic illness) of such intensity that adequate cooperation in the examination is not possible.
-The informed consent form was not signed.
